primary_flora: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas (Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon, 1999)
method: Research annotations only; preserve exact historical flora names/pages; distinguish alternate FNA and existing FNA-based research values; BONAP county statuses unchanged.

records.historical_name: Euphorbia eriantha Benth. (1999 species treatment not located)
records.source: Flora of North America, Euphorbia eriantha

morphology.habit: Annual or short-lived perennial, erect to ascending, reported 10–75 cm in repository's FNA-backed profile
morphology.leaves: Mostly alternate, narrow linear to linear-elliptic, 20–55 × 1–3 mm, occasionally 2–4 small distal teeth
morphology.cyathia: Involucre obconic 2.1–2.6 × 1.3–2 mm, gray-white hairy; 2–5, usually 4–5 glands 0.5–0.6 × 0.5–0.6 mm; white hooded incurved gland appendages 0.5–1 × 0.5–0.8 mm, each divided into 5–12 narrow fringed segments
morphology.fruit: Three-lobed oblong-ovoid capsule, repository FNA-based 4.4–4.9 × 3.5–4.1 mm, densely pale-hairy
morphology.seeds: Repository FNA-based 2.8–4.1 × 2–2.4 mm, tuberculate or pitted with a caruncle
morphology.habitat: Rocky desert washes and slopes; Hays occurrence not established

records.diagnostics: The unusual fringed white appendages curl over the glands; do not mistake these for ordinary petals
holds: Not found as a species treatment in 1999 flora; source measurements are FNA-derived, not 1999
County BONAP native range not verified
records.roots: See habit when documented; otherwise unreported in cited species description

morphology.habit: Perennial with woody roots; rather wiry prostrate to spreading or ascending stems to 20 cm
morphology.leaves: Orbicular-ovate to oblong; entire, acute apex
morphology.cyathia: Styles bifid for at least half their length, gland appendages variable per FNA
morphology.habitat: Rocky or sandy soils; flora lists Bell, Bosque, Tarrant, Brown and Hamilton counties
morphology.fruit: FNA-backed existing profile: glabrous depressed-globose capsule 2–2.4 × 2.2–2.5 mm
morphology.seeds: FNA-backed existing profile: white 4-angled seed 1.7–2 × 1–1.2 mm

records.diagnostics: Woody-rooted perennial sandmat with mostly low glabrous shoots and entire small leaves; flowers' appendage morphology is highly variable
holds: Fruit and seed measurements from modern FNA-backed profile, not 1999 flora
records.roots: See habit when documented; otherwise unreported in cited species description

records.historical_name: Chamaesyce golondrina (L.C.Wheeler) Shinners; no matching 1999 species treatment located
records.source: Flora of North America, Euphorbia golondrina

morphology.habit: Annual with glabrous prostrate stems 5–35 cm
morphology.leaves: Opposite, oblong to ovate-oblong, 5–11.5 × 1–4 mm, entire and asymmetric-based
morphology.cyathia: Solitary at distal nodes; dark red-purple concave glands with white crescent appendages; peduncles 0.9–1.5 mm
morphology.seeds: Four-angled approximately 1.3–1.5 × 0.6–0.7 mm, weak cross ridges
morphology.habitat: Sandy/gravelly Rio Grande banks in western Texas; FNA notes highly restricted border distribution

records.diagnostics: Glabrous prostrate sandmat with dark round glands and pale crescent appendages; comparison to E. simulans requires glands and seeds
holds: Not a presumptively native Hays species; verify BONAP county eligibility separately
Quantitative traits drawn from existing FNA-based profile; revisit original FNA text for full verification
records.roots: See habit when documented; otherwise unreported in cited species description

records.historical_name: Euphorbia heterophylla L. (1999 species account not located)
records.source: Flora of North America, Euphorbia heterophylla

morphology.leaves: Usually alternate and polymorphic: lanceolate, elliptic, obovate, pandurate or lobed; leaf outline alone unreliable
morphology.bracts: Terminal bracts predominantly green or light green rather than distinctly red-based
morphology.cyathia: Usually one stalked clavate yellow-green nectar gland, circular opening with annular rim; gland appendages absent
morphology.fruit: Three-lobed broadly ovoid capsule 2.8–3.8 × 4–5.3 mm, generally glabrous
morphology.seeds: Angular tuberculate seed 2.4–2.8 × 1.9–2.4 mm, keel along dorsal face

records.diagnostics: Compare E. cyathophora: cyathophora often sharply red/pink proximal bracts, gland aperture oblong and rim absent; heterophylla circular annular-rimmed gland
holds: 1999 original account not identified; FNA quantitative character extraction is retained from prior repository research
Native zone remains comparison-only, not county-approved
records.roots: See habit when documented; otherwise unreported in cited species description

morphology.habit: Main stem erect to 50 cm, branches erect or ascending
morphology.leaves: Usually without a central purple-red spot
morphology.cyathia: Dense conspicuous glomerules with white-to-pink gland appendages; styles bifid to midpoint
morphology.fruit: 1999 key: capsules approximately 1.3 mm, versus E. nutans 1.9–2.3 mm
morphology.habitat: In 1999 flora: sidewalk, horticultural nursery/garden weed in Tarrant County, mainly southern Texas

records.diagnostics: Crowded glomerules, glabrous stems, relatively small capsules distinguish from leafy cyathium clusters and often line-hairy E. nutans
holds: Flora calls it native to extreme southern Texas and an introduced Fort Worth weed, not a Hays native record
records.roots: See habit when documented; otherwise unreported in cited species description

morphology.habit: Annual, prostrate or rarely ascending, stems to 50 cm, does not root at nodes
morphology.leaves: Opposite, small, finely toothed oblong blades, often with purple-red central blotch but this may be absent
morphology.cyathia: Gland appendages white to red, styles bifid upper quarter to third
morphology.fruit: 1999 key: capsule hairs rather evenly distributed across face and loosely appressed, versus E. prostrata hairs more spreading along angles
morphology.seeds: Modern FNA-based repository: approximately 1–1.2 mm, angular with several low transverse ridges, NOT longitudinal ribbing
morphology.habitat: Sandy soils, stream banks, woods and disturbed areas; much of Texas

records.diagnostics: Capsule face hair distribution is more reliable than leaf blotches; fruit comparison with E. prostrata
holds: Historical name 'Chamaesyce maculata' commonly confused with C. nutans in older reports
Corrected transverse seed ridges preserved; seed measurements from modern profile
records.roots: See habit when documented; otherwise unreported in cited species description

morphology.habit: Pilose to glabrous erect annual to about 200 cm
morphology.leaves: Stem foliage often relatively broad, showy upper leaves/bracts prominently white-edged
morphology.cyathia: Usually five cupped glands, white petal-like appendages 2–4 mm
morphology.fruit: Three-lobed capsule, hairy; latex may irritate skin
morphology.habitat: Calcareous uplands, streams and low places

records.diagnostics: Compared with E. bicolor, usually broader upper bracts and little hair on the upper blade surface; narrow bracts alone can appear within one inflorescence
holds: 1999 reports eastern native regional limit roughly Bell to Cooke counties but this does not substitute for BONAP county map
records.roots: See habit when documented; otherwise unreported in cited species description

morphology.habit: Annual, one to several decumbent, spreading or erect stems up to 1 m
morphology.stems: Pubescent in longitudinal lines; different from generally glabrous E. hypericifolia
morphology.leaves: Oblong and asymmetrical, often (not always) purple-red central blotch
morphology.cyathia: White-to-reddish gland appendages, styles bifid to approximately halfway
morphology.fruit: 1999 key glabrous capsule 1.9–2.3 mm, often solitary/small clusters of cyathia
morphology.habitat: Stream bottoms, roadsides and disturbed soils, throughout Texas

records.diagnostics: More robust ascending branches and less congested cyathium clusters than E. hypericifolia; historical C. maculata sensu authors often refers to C. nutans
holds: Do not infer species from red foliar splotches, frequently present in E. maculata as well
records.roots: See habit when documented; otherwise unreported in cited species description

records.historical_name: Euphorbia ophthalmica Pers. / Chamaesyce ophthalmica (Pers.) D.G.Burch
records.source: Flora of North America, Euphorbia ophthalmica

morphology.habit: Low prostrate herb, often annual, typically shoots 6–22 cm per repository FNA-backed description
morphology.leaves: Opposite, unequal bases, ovate to oblong 4–13 × 3–7 mm; serrulate; three basal veins common
morphology.stems: Short appressed hairs mixed with longer spreading hairs
morphology.cyathia: Dense compact terminal headlike glomerules, instead of scattered axillary cyathia
morphology.fruit: Small ovoid hairy capsule ca. 1–1.2 × 1–1.3 mm
morphology.seeds: Approximately 0.7–0.9(–1.1) × 0.5 mm, four-angled with weak transverse wrinkles

records.diagnostics: Dense terminal headlike cyathia, mixed hair lengths and serrulate small leaves; comparison with E. hirta requires reproductive axis context
holds: Not located in 1999 flora and regional nativity uncertain
Full FNA measurements inherited from existing research profile; source review pending
records.roots: See habit when documented; otherwise unreported in cited species description

morphology.leaves: Small broadly elliptic leaves usually lack reddish central spot (variable)
morphology.cyathia: Styles forked to base or near base
morphology.fruit: Per 1999 key, capsule spreading-pubescent, hairs largely along angles; unlike uniformly hairy capsule faces in E. maculata
morphology.seeds: FNA-backed existing profile: sharply four-angled, about 0.8–1.1 × 0.5–0.7 mm, distinct transverse ribs
morphology.habitat: Stream banks, prairies, disturbed clay-rich ground, most of Texas

records.diagnostics: Prostrate mat, hairy capsule edges and prominent narrow transverse seed ribs; do not rely on spot absence alone
holds: County BONAP target status stays provisional
Fruit/seed microscopy more useful than habit and spot
